title: Byeonhan
capsule: Byeonhan (변진, 弁韓) was a loose confederacy of a dozen or more chiefdoms occupying the lower Nakdong River basin in the southern Korean peninsula, attested from the late second century BCE. Distinguished from its neighbors Mahan and Jinhan primarily by dialect and custom, Byeonhan was notable for high-quality iron production exported to Lelang Commandery and the Wa of Japan, functioning as an early regional entrepôt. The confederacy gradually coalesced into the Gaya confederation by the early centuries CE, with the transformation completed by roughly the fourth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Byeonhan is attested primarily in the Chinese Sanguozhi and Korean samguk sources, but territorial extents of individual chiefdoms are only approximately reconstructable.

rulers.name: (no named individual rulers attested; confederacy of twelve statelets led by unnamed chiefs)
